theory.intro: Divide any circle's circumference by its diameter and the answer is always the same number, a little more than $3$. That number is called $\pi$, said "pi".
facts: $\pi = \frac{C}{d}$, where $C$ is the circumference and $d$ is the diameter of the **same** circle.
The decimal $\pi = 3.14159\ldots$ never ends and never repeats, so the exact value is written as the symbol $\pi$.
The ratio is the **same for every circle**: a wider circle has a bigger circumference and diameter, so the division gives the same answer.
Because $C \div d$ is a little more than $3$, the diameter fits **just over $3$ times** around the circumference.
Measurements are never perfectly accurate, so a measured $C \div d$ comes out **close to** $3.14$ rather than exactly $3.14$.

workedExamples.question_text:
Two circular objects were measured.
a) The first has circumference $53.3$ cm and diameter $17$ cm.
b) The second has circumference $56.5$ cm and radius $9$ cm.
Calculate $C \div d$ for each, correct to $2$ decimal places.
workedExamples.solution_text:
a)
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{C}{d}\\&=\frac{53.3}{17}\\&=3.135294\ldots\\&\approx3.14\end{aligned}$
b) $d = 2 \times 9 = 18$ cm.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{C}{d}\\&=\frac{56.5}{18}\\&=3.138888\ldots\\&\approx3.14\end{aligned}$
Both measurements give an estimate close to $\pi$.

workedExamples.question_text:
Three circular objects were measured.
$\begin{array}{c|c|c} \text{Object} & C\text{ (cm)} & d\text{ (cm)} \\ \hline A & 22.0 & 7 \\ B & 59.7 & 19 \\ C & 46.8 & 13 \end{array}$
a) Calculate $C \div d$ for each, correct to $2$ decimal places.
b) Explain why the different sizes of A and B do not give different values of $\pi$.
c) Which object has a measurement far from its correct value?
workedExamples.solution_text:
a) A: $\frac{22.0}{7} = 3.142857\ldots \approx 3.14$
B: $\frac{59.7}{19} = 3.142105\ldots \approx 3.14$
C: $\frac{46.8}{13} = 3.6 = 3.60$
b) For every circle, the circumference divided by the diameter is the same number, $\pi$.
Both A and B give measured ratios close to $\pi$.
c) Object C gives $3.60$, far from $3.14$, so one of its measurements is inaccurate.

a) $\pi = \frac{C}{d}$.
b) Since $\pi = 3.14159\ldots$, just over $3$ diameter lengths fit around the circumference.
The radius is half the diameter, so dividing by the radius doubles the answer: $\frac{C}{r} = 2\pi$.
c) $\pi = 3.14159\ldots$
To $3$ decimal places, $\pi \approx 3.142$.
To $4$ decimal places, $\pi \approx 3.1416$.

foundation.question_text:
A circle has circumference $18.84$ cm and diameter $6$ cm.
Use these measurements to find an approximate value for $\pi$, correct to $2$ decimal places.

A circle has circumference $28.27$ cm and diameter $9$ cm.
Use these measurements to find an approximate value for $\pi$, correct to $2$ decimal places.

A circle has circumference $C$ and diameter $d$.
Write down the calculation that gives $\pi$.
foundation.solution_text:
$\pi$ is the circumference divided by the diameter of the same circle.
$\pi = \frac{C}{d}$

foundation.question_text:
A piece of string is cut the same length as a circle's diameter.
About how many of these strings are needed to go once around the circumference?
foundation.solution_text:
The circumference divided by the diameter is always $\pi = 3.14159\ldots$
Just over $3$ of them are needed.

development.question_text:
A circle has circumference $38.95$ cm and diameter $12.4$ cm.
Use these measurements to find an approximate value for $\pi$, correct to $2$ decimal places.

development.solution_text:
Circle A: $\frac{C}{d} = \frac{9.42}{3} = 3.14$
Circle B: $\frac{C}{d} = \frac{37.70}{12} = 3.1416\ldots \approx 3.14$
Both measured ratios round to $3.14$, even though circle B is four times as wide.
For every circle, the exact ratio is $\pi$.

development.question_text:
Circle A has circumference $14.14$ cm and diameter $4.5$ cm.
Circle B has circumference $70.69$ cm and diameter $22.5$ cm.
Calculate $C \div d$ for each circle, correct to $2$ decimal places, and state what you notice.
development.solution_text:
Circle A: $\frac{14.14}{4.5} = 3.142222\ldots \approx 3.14$
Circle B: $\frac{70.69}{22.5} = 3.141777\ldots \approx 3.14$
Both measured ratios round to $3.14$, even though the circles have different sizes.
For every circle, the exact ratio is $\pi$.

development.question_text:
A lid is rolled along a ruler for exactly one complete turn and the roll measures $18.8$ cm.
The lid's diameter is $6$ cm.
How many diameters fit into the roll length?
Give your answer correct to $1$ decimal place.

Is $\pi = \frac{d}{C}$ a correct definition?
Explain your answer.
development.solution_text:
$\pi$ is the circumference divided by the diameter, not the other way around.
Dividing the diameter by the circumference gives $\frac{1}{\pi} = 0.318\ldots$, which is less than $1$.
No, the correct definition is $\pi = \frac{C}{d}$.

mastery.question_text:
Four circles were measured in class.
$\begin{array}{c|c|c} \text{Circle} & C\text{ (mm)} & d\text{ (mm)} \\ \hline P & 36.13 & 11.5 \\ Q & 86.39 & 27.5 \\ R & 136.66 & 43.5 \\ S & 249.76 & 79.5 \end{array}$
Calculate $C \div d$ for each circle, correct to $2$ decimal places, and state what you notice.
mastery.solution_text:
P: $\frac{36.13}{11.5} = 3.141739\ldots \approx 3.14$
Q: $\frac{86.39}{27.5} = 3.141454\ldots \approx 3.14$
R: $\frac{136.66}{43.5} = 3.141609\ldots \approx 3.14$
S: $\frac{249.76}{79.5} = 3.141635\ldots \approx 3.14$
All four measured ratios round to $3.14$, even though the circles have different sizes.
For every circle, the exact ratio is $\pi$.

Circle A: $\frac{25.13}{8} = 3.1412\ldots \approx 3.14$
Circle B: $\frac{157.08}{50} = 3.1416 \approx 3.14$
Circle B is more than six times as wide, but its circumference is more than six times as long as well.
The two increases cancel in the division, so every circle gives the same ratio $\pi$.
